thesis: The Qur'an forbids turning one's back when the battle lines meet but permits only movements that still serve the fight, exposing every other retreat as fear breaking a communal trust.
notes: ORIGINAL FLAG RESOLVED. The added section 'The dispute al-Tabari spends most of his commentary on' checks out attribution by attribution against the fetched al-Tabari. Badr-specific camp: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (athar 15798-15801, via Abu Nadrah: 'innama kana dhalika yawma Badr'), al-Hasan (15805 'kanat hadhihi yawma Badr khassatan', 15807, 15809), Qatadah (15808 'dhalikum yawma Badr'), ad-Dahhak (15804, 15806 'kanat hadhihi yawma Badr khassatan'), Nafi' (15803 and 15810, Ibn 'Awn's letter: 'innama kana dhalika yawma Badr') - all five verified. 'Ata b. Abi Rabah via Qays b. Sa'd (15813) reads it through the 8:66 takhfif and says 'wa laysa li-qawmin an yafirru min mithlayhim' - the file renders this as the ruling being 'lightened by 8:66, which removes the obligation to stand against more than twice one's number', an accurate rendering of the position ('Ata's own word is 'mansukhah', partial naskh 'illa hadhihi al-'iddah'; the file's paraphrase tracks the effect, does not distort it). Ibn 'Abbas for the general reading verified under al-Tabari's own heading 'wa qala akharun: bal hadhihi al-ayah hukmuha 'amm' (15816, via 'Ali b. Abi Talha: 'akbar al-kaba'ir al-shirk bi-llah wa al-firar min al-zahf'). The seven-destructive-sins hadith (al-Bukhari/Muslim, Abu Hurayrah) is carried in the fetched Ibn Kathir, and includes 'al-tawalli yawm al-zahf' - the file does not attribute it to al-Tabari, so no mismatch. Al-Tabari's tarjih verified verbatim in substance: 'wa awla al-ta'wilayn fi hadhihi al-ayah bi-l-sawab 'indi qawl man qala: hukmuha muhkam, wa annaha nazalat fi ahl Badr, wa hukmuha thabit fi jami' al-mu'minin', with the two exceptions (tahrif li-qital / tahayyuz ila fi'ah) named. The claim that mainstream fiqh incorporates the 8:66 two-to-one limit is independently supported by the fetched al-Jalalayn on 8:16: 'wa hadha makhsus bima idha lam yazid al-kuffar 'ala al-di'f'. The section-title claim that this dispute occupies most of al-Tabari's commentary is fair - athar 15797-15816 are almost entirely that question. Tadabbur-vs-fatwa line present and explicit. The batch5 minor flag ('Anything else is not strategic humility. It is a surrender of trust.') is also cured, since the new section now names the 8:66 concession as a limit. No truncation artifacts; verify_arabic 2/2 and verify_morphology 20/20 pass.

thesis: The Qur'an commands believers to prepare force with full seriousness as deterrence while remaining inwardly free to accept genuine peace, holding both readiness and peace under tawakkul.
notes: ORIGINAL FLAG RESOLVED. The added section 'The verse about peace, and the argument over whether it still stands' verifies against the fetched editions. Naskh camp in al-Tabari on 8:61: Qatadah (16245 'wa nasakhaha qawluhu fa-qtulu al-mushrikin haythu wajadtumuhum'; 16246 'wa kanat hadhihi qabla Bara'ah ... thumma nusikha dhalika ba'du fi Bara'ah'), 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri together (16247 'nasakhatha al-ayah allati fi Bara'ah', citing 9:29), Ibn Zayd (16250 'wa hadha qad nasakhahu al-jihad') - all four verified as holding naskh. Note for the record: Ibn Zayd's reported abrogator is 'al-jihad' rather than Bara'ah by name; al-Tabari himself groups the whole camp as 'ma qalahu Qatadah wa man qala mithla qawlihi' and answers it with Bara'ah 9:5, so the file's grouping is a fair compression, not a misattribution. Al-Jalalayn verified verbatim: 'wa qala Ibn 'Abbas: hadha mansukh bi-ayat al-sayf wa qala Mujahid: makhsus bi-ahl al-kitab idh nazalat fi Bani Qurayzah' - both the Ibn 'Abbas naskh citation and the Mujahid restriction check out; the file's 'restricting the verse to Banu Qurayzah' is the compressed form of Jalalayn's clause and is independently matched by al-Tabari 16251 (Mujahid: 'Qurayzah'), and the file's very next sentence supplies the ahl al-kitab dimension, so the reader is not misled. Al-Tabari's rejection verified: 'fa-qawlun la dalalata 'alayhi min kitabin wa la sunnatin wa la fitrati 'aql' - the file paraphrases 'no evidence for it from the Book or the Sunnah' without quotation marks and without claiming completeness, so the dropped 'wa la fitrati 'aql' is not a misquote. His scope restriction verified: 'innama 'uniya bihi Banu Qurayzah, wa kanu yahudan ahl kitab, wa qad adhina Allah ... bi-sulh ahl al-kitab ... 'ala akhdh al-jizyah minhum'. Ibn Kathir's Hudaybiyah material verified ('when the pagans inclined to peace in the year of Hudaybiyah ... he accepted this from them'), plus the 'Ali report 'if you have a way to end them in peace, then do so'. Critically, the section states outright that the reflection follows al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir and that this 'is a choice among classical positions, not the only reading on offer' - the universal-standing-command framing is now disclosed as a position rather than asserted as the meaning. The batch6 minor flag ('Strength is obligatory. Readiness matters.') is cured by the closing sentence naming i'dad as a matter of fiqh with conditions and stating this is tadabbur, not fatwa. No truncation artifacts; verify_arabic 3/3 and verify_morphology 23/23 pass.
